candidate.blueprint_locator: Management of Care → Advocacy/Client Rights/Case Management/Performance Improvement: assist clients in accessing grievance or advocacy resources, coordinate care and referrals, and participate in quality-improvement processes that affect client care.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — ESRD Network grievance, advocacy, and quality-improvement functions
candidate.educational_objective: Use the CMS ESRD Network as an advocacy and quality-improvement resource when a dialysis client has unresolved grievances or access-to-care concerns.

options.A: The regional ESRD Network can help evaluate and resolve patient grievances and access-to-care issues and also works with patients and providers on quality improvement; it does not replace the treating dialysis facility.
options.B: The ESRD Network directly provides the client's routine dialysis treatments and replaces the dialysis facility when a grievance occurs.
options.C: The ESRD Network is limited to research and data collection and has no role in patient grievances, care coordination, or quality improvement.
options.D: The ESRD Network handles only Medicare billing disputes and cannot assist with concerns about dialysis care or access to services.

candidate.rationale: CMS states that ESRD Network Organizations are regional organizations that help coordinate ESRD services and act as liaisons between patients, providers, and the federal government. Statutory Network responsibilities include implementing procedures for evaluating and resolving patient grievances, conducting quality and appropriateness activities, collecting and analyzing data, and helping facilities correct quality problems. Under the current 13th Scope of Work for 2026-2031, Networks also emphasize patient/family choice, care coordination, access to care, quality improvement, and data-driven improvements. Therefore, A is correct. Networks do not directly replace the client's dialysis provider, are not limited to research, and are not merely billing-dispute organizations.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Directly supports ESRD Networks as regional CMS-contracted organizations involved in grievance resolution, patient advocacy/access-to-care support, quality improvement, care coordination, and data activities rather than direct provision of routine dialysis treatment.
candidate.source_document_title: End Stage Renal Disease (ESRD) Network Programs
candidate.source_locator: CMS 'End Stage Renal Disease (ESRD) Network Programs' → 'Why does CMS have an ESRD Network Program?': Network Organizations develop quality/appropriateness criteria, evaluate treatment-modality processes, implement procedures for evaluating and resolving patient grievances, conduct on-site reviews when necessary, collect/validate/analyze data, maintain the patient registry, and assist noncooperating facilities with corrective action. '2026-2031 Activities': patient/family choice, care coordination, access to care, quality improvement and interoperability/data initiatives.
candidate.source_version_date: 13th Scope of Work 2026-2031; CMS page last modified 2026-05-29
candidate.stem: A client receiving chronic dialysis says, "I have tried to resolve a care grievance with my dialysis facility but still need help. What can the ESRD Network do?" Which response by the nurse is most accurate?
